Large fluorescence quantum yields can result from large radiative rate constants, very inefficient nonradiative relaxation processes, or both. Let’s see how the values of the individual rate constants can be estimated from the measured values of fluorescence quantum yields. Radiative rate constants are formally related to absorption cross sections through the Einstein radiation relations (see Section 20.8) and we established an empirical relationship between the magnitudes of ab- sorption cross sections and those of molar absorption coefficients earlier.
